synopsis: An Image miniseries featuring the classic golden-age character Airboy in a modern setting, this smaller companion to the main Airboy revival exploring secondary characters from the World War II aviation hero mythology. Niche appeal for fans of the main series.
author: Chuck Dixon, Gianluca Piredda

subject: series
synopsis: A comedic all-ages adventure series reimagining Albert Einstein as a secret time-traveling agent who uses his scientific genius to protect history. The book plays its absurd premise for lighthearted fun with clever historical Easter eggs.
author: Marcus Perry

subject: series
synopsis: Léo's acclaimed Brazilian-born Franco-Belgian sci-fi series set on a colony planet, following Kim Keller's survival and discovery of a vast alien ecosystem; the first arc of the larger Worlds of Aldebaran cycle, praised for its detailed alien biology and human drama.
author: Léo

subject: series
synopsis: A licensed comic featuring the legendary shock-rock musician Alice Cooper, blending his horror-themed stage persona with comic book storytelling in a dark, theatrical adventure series.
author: Rodney Barnes

subject: series
synopsis: Iolanda Zanfardino and Elisa Romboli's queer romantic comedy: a heartbroken young woman leaves her small town for San Francisco in search of true love.
author: Iolanda Zanfardino

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite's comics adaptation of Lewis Carroll's classic fantasy tale, presenting Alice's adventures in Wonderland in a new visual interpretation for comics readers.

subject: series
synopsis: A return to the classic Marvel/Epic Comics military sci-fi series Alien Legion, following the multispecies mercenary unit Force Nomad. Published by Titan.
author: Chuck Dixon, Carl Potts

subject: series
synopsis: A classic DC war anthology series running from the 1950s through the early 1970s, featuring stories of American servicemen across various conflicts. Alongside Our Army at War and G.I. Combat, it defined DC's golden era of war comics.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: James Robinson and Steve Pugh's Marvel series reunites the surviving World War II-era Invaders — Captain America, Namor, the original Human Torch, and Bucky — when a Kree plot tied to their past resurfaces. A legacy-minded team book bridging Marvel's Golden Age and present.
author: James Robinson

subject: series
synopsis: Paul Jenkins' limited series exploring the untold history of the WWII-era All-Winners Squad, Marvel's golden age super-team, framed through a contemporary soldier's investigation into the heroes who shaped the Allied war effort.
author: Paul Jenkins

subject: series
synopsis: A thriller about an undocumented immigrant navigating dangerous circumstances in contemporary America, blending political commentary with personal stakes. Aftershock's socially conscious edge applied to immigration themes.
author: Ron Marz

subject: series
synopsis: B. Clay Moore's return to the Hawaiian Dick universe follows the same 1950s Honolulu setting with a new case, delivering more of the series' distinctive blend of hardboiled noir and Hawaiian supernatural.
author: B. Clay Moore

subject: series
synopsis: Tom DeFalco's continuation of the MC2 Spider-Girl series following May 'Mayday' Parker, the teenage daughter of Peter Parker, as she balances high school life with the responsibilities of being Spider-Girl. A fan-beloved series kept alive for years by reader loyalty campaigns.
author: Tom DeFalco

subject: series
synopsis: A year-long Amazing Spider-Man arc where Ben Reilly returned as Spider-Man while Peter Parker was incapacitated, exploring corporate superheroics through the Beyond Corporation's ownership of the Spider-Man brand.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Jen Van Meter's limited series spotlighting Felicia Hardy as she navigates the criminal underworld of the Marvel Universe, showcasing Black Cat's morally ambiguous nature and the tension between her thieving lifestyle and her complicated feelings for Spider-Man.
author: Jen Van Meter

subject: series
synopsis: Ultimate Collection trade paperback reprints of J. Michael Straczynski's celebrated Amazing Spider-Man run, which revitalized the character with mystical mythology, mature themes, and the controversial but memorable Sins Past arc. One of the most discussed Spidey runs of the 2000s.
author: J. Michael Straczynski

subject: series
synopsis: MC2 universe limited series featuring Shannon Carter, the niece of Sharon Carter, who takes up the Captain America legacy in the alternate future where heroes have retired or passed on. Tom DeFalco's earnest take on a legacy hero.
author: Tom DeFalco

subject: series
synopsis: An anthology series reimagining iconic American folklore and tall-tale characters.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Claudio Sanchez of Coheed and Cambria's comic adaptation of the science fiction mythology underpinning his band's concept albums, depicting the dystopian world of the Keywork and its tragic hero Claudio Kilgannon. An ambitious cosmic sci-fi epic with genuine world-building that rewards fans of the albums deeply.
author: Claudio Sanchez

subject: series
synopsis: ComixTribe's breakout horror series by John Lees and Iain Laurie follows a haunted former detective investigating the disappearance of a girl on a remote Scottish island, delivering folk-horror dread with nightmarish expressionist art.
author: John Lees

subject: series
synopsis: Scott Tipton's Angel spinoff set after the IDW comics era follows Gunn in a story exploring his humanity and loyalty to Angel's mission.
author: Scott Tipton

subject: series
synopsis: Chris Grine's faithful graphic novel adaptation of K.A. Applegate's beloved 1990s YA sci-fi novel, following five teenagers given the ability to morph into any animal they touch to fight a secret alien invasion. Grine's energetic art captures the horror and wonder of transformation that made the original series iconic.
author: K.A. Applegate

subject: series
synopsis: A four-issue miniseries following a heavyweight cosmic team assembled to be a preemptive strike force - including Ronan, Silver Surfer, Beta Ray Bill, Gladiator, and Quasar - a spiritual successor to the Annihilation-era cosmic renaissance.
author: Dan Abnett

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Abnett and Andy Lanning's limited series bringing Marvel's cosmic heavy-hitters - including Quasar, Ronan, and the Silver Surfer - down to Earth to face a planetary threat, serving as a coda to the Annihilation era of cosmic Marvel storytelling.
author: Dan Abnett
artist: Timothy Green II, Tan Eng Huat

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Waid's limited series pairing Scott Lang's Ant-Man with Nadia Van Dyne's Wasp in a dimension-hopping adventure that plays up the comedic chemistry between the two shrinking heroes while delivering accessible family-friendly superhero action.
author: Mark Waid

subject: series
synopsis: A mid-1980s Fantagraphics anthology showcasing alternative and underground cartoonists of the era, serving as a showcase for the then-emerging literary comics scene that Fantagraphics was building during the crucial transition from underground comix to alternative comics.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Michael Avon Oeming's limited series exploring Ares' transition from villain to reluctant antihero, delving into his mythological background and his complicated relationship with his son Phobos, laying groundwork for his later Mighty Avengers membership.
author: Michael Avon Oeming

subject: series
synopsis: Valiant's 2022 limited series introduces new armored warriors to the Valiant universe, delivering superhero action with the publisher's characteristic seriousness.
author: Evan Narcisse

subject: series
synopsis: A comedic crossover mini-series uniting Ash Williams and Xena the Warrior Princess against supernatural threats, delivering the anachronistic action-comedy the mashup premise promises to fans of both franchises.

subject: series
synopsis: Two women from different eras -- a World War II spy and a modern-day assassin -- are thrown together through a time-travel mechanism and must work together despite their conflicting goals. A kinetic action series with a strong female duo at its center.
author: Stephanie Phillips

subject: series
synopsis: A survival horror manga by Muneyuki Kaneshiro and Akeji Fujimura about high school students suddenly forced to participate in deadly games based on children's toys and folklore, orchestrated by mysterious supernatural beings. A tense, inventive twist on the Battle Royale survival genre with creative game designs and high stakes.
author: Muneyuki Kaneshiro

subject: series
synopsis: Jeff Lemire and Dustin Nguyen's sequel to Descender: a generation later, technology is banned and magic rules the universe. The painterly art style carries over perfectly; Lemire's emotional core remains strong.
author: Jeff Lemire

subject: series
synopsis: Tini Howard and Gilbert Hernandez's action series about retired female assassins drawn back into the life. Gloriously pulpy with Hernandez bringing his Palomar sensibility to hired-killer action.
author: Tini Howard

subject: series
synopsis: An astronaut returning from a mission finds himself displaced across multiple versions of reality, unsure which world is home. Jonathan hat Reed's Aftershock series explores identity and belonging through a sci-fi lens.
author: Jonathan Hat Reed

subject: series
synopsis: Saki Nakagawa's parody spin-off of the main Attack on Titan series, reimagining the characters as students at a middle school where the titans are athletic rivals rather than existential threats. Gag-manga territory for fans of the main series.
author: Saki Nakagawa

subject: series
synopsis: Trade paperback collections of Brian Michael Bendis' post-Heroic Age Avengers run, featuring a classic lineup including Captain America, Iron Man, and Thor in globe-spanning adventures. A solid if uneven period following Bendis' landmark earlier work on the team.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: A recent miniseries pairing Janet Van Dyne and Victor Shade (the Vision) as detective partners investigating a mystery within the Marvel Universe, offering a noir-inflected take on Avengers legacy characters with strong character chemistry.
author: Al Ewing

subject: series
synopsis: A modern action-driven series featuring giant robot mechanics and superhero warfare.
author: Jed MacKay

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Clevinger and Brian Churilla's all-ages retelling of the Infinity Gauntlet storyline, condensing the cosmic epic into a fun and accessible adventure for younger readers while preserving the high stakes of the original Thanos saga.
author: Brian Clevinger

subject: series
synopsis: A four-issue anthology tie-in to the AXIS event, presenting stories of characters whose moral alignment was inverted by the Red Skull's use of the Scarlet Witch and Professor X's combined psychic power.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A Zenescope action series featuring a female protagonist in a bar or tavern setting, likely with supernatural or action-adventure elements consistent with the publisher's mature fantasy line.
author: Joe Brusha, Clayburn Moore

subject: series
synopsis: Kaito Toka's tender manga about an elderly woman who discovers boys' love manga and bonds with the teenage girl who works at the bookstore, as they explore a new genre together and form an unlikely friendship across generations. Understated, sweet, and surprisingly moving.
author: Kaito Toka

subject: series
synopsis: A modern indie series from Ahoy Comics.
author: Garth Ennis, James Finn Garner

subject: series
synopsis: Donny Cates and Garry Brown's horror series about a teenager who discovers she's given birth to the Antichrist and chooses to protect her baby from the dark forces that want to use him. Cates writes with genuine emotional investment in the parent-child relationship.
author: Donny Cates

subject: series
synopsis: Eddie Campbell's long-running mythological comedy series follows Bacchus, the ancient god of wine, surviving into the modern world surrounded by other mythological figures. A landmark of indie comics, blending classical mythology with modern gritty street life, mixing humor with pathos. Collected in five volumes by Top Shelf.
author: Eddie Campbell

subject: series
synopsis: Jimmy Palmiotti, Garth Ennis, and Mihailo Vukelic's crime thriller about a mob enforcer who goes rogue to rescue his kidnapped family from the New York crime syndicate he used to work for. Ennis's trademark hardboiled dialogue elevates what might otherwise be a familiar crime premise.
author: Garth Ennis

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Maberry and Tyler Crook's vampire horror following a cancer patient who, after being bitten by a vampire, discovers his terminal illness makes his blood toxic to the undead — turning him into an unlikely vampire hunter with nothing to lose. Sharp dark comedy meets body horror.
author: Jonathan Maberry

subject: series
synopsis: Juan Doe's solo creator series about a group stranded on a remote island during a bachelorette party, who begin dying off one by one while cut off from civilization. Doe writes and draws with striking graphic economy.
author: Juan Doe

subject: series
synopsis: Adam Egypt Mortimer and Darick Robertson's sci-fi action story set in a future where biology and technology have merged in grotesque ways, following a courier whose weapon is a sentient gun with its own personality. Robertson's detailed artwork in an unusual setting.
author: Adam Egypt Mortimer

subject: series
synopsis: Brian K. Vaughan and Marcos Martin's immigration story about a Honduran woman and a Texas rancher thrown together by an alien encounter. Told partly in untranslated Spanish, forcing readers into the immigrant experience. Provocative and visually inventive.
author: Brian K. Vaughan

subject: series
synopsis: DC's long-running series of Batman oversized annuals, featuring notable stories including Neal Adams artwork in early issues and various significant one-off tales across decades.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A limited series crossover between DC's Batman and the Italian horror/mystery character Dylan Dog, pairing the Dark Knight with the British paranormal investigator in a supernatural mystery set in Gotham City.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: G. Willow Wilson and Jamie McKelvie's prestige one-shot: Selina Kyle plans a heist to settle a score from her past.

subject: series
synopsis: A holiday crossover limited series pairing Batman with Santa Claus in an absurdist adventure, part of DC's seasonal publishing output.

subject: series
synopsis: A five-issue limited series by Sam Kieth in which Batman pursues a serial killer while a photographer uses the Caped Crusader's violent methods to question whether heroes and monsters are different. Kieth's expressionistic art style makes it visually distinctive.
author: Sam Kieth

subject: series
synopsis: A four-issue prestige format mini-series by Jim Starlin and Bernie Wrightson in which Batman is captured and psychologically broken by the cult leader Deacon Blackfire, who has turned Gotham's homeless into a fanatical army. Wrightson's painted art gives it a uniquely horrific quality.
author: Jim Starlin

subject: series
synopsis: A digital-first comic tie-in to the 2016 Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice film, providing supplementary story content set in the movie's continuity.

subject: series
synopsis: Chuck Dixon's 4-issue miniseries focuses on Commissioner Gordon's pre-Batman career, examining his history with organized crime and the moral compromises that shaped Gotham's most upright cop. A solid character study that enriches Gordon without needing Batman at its center.
author: Chuck Dixon

subject: series
synopsis: Trade collections of late-1980s and early-90s Batman, including Alan Grant and Norm Breyfogle's Detective run and Marv Wolfman's tenure.
author: Alan Grant, Marv Wolfman

subject: series
synopsis: Archival reprints of Batman's earliest adventures from the 1930s and 1940s.
author: Bob Kane

subject: series
synopsis: B. Clay Moore and Jeremy Haun's WWII superhero revisionist story featuring an American team of costumed heroes during the war, examining the darker reality behind the patriotic myth of golden age superheroism with gritty period authenticity.
author: B. Clay Moore
